hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: Extract the hour from call_time using hour extraction and aggregate count of calls grouped by city and hour.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Use window ranking partitioned by city and ordered by number of calls descending to handle ties.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Filter for rank = 1 and order by peak_calling_hour descending, then city descending.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH CityHourCount AS (
    SELECT 
        city, 
        HOUR(call_time) AS peak_calling_hour, 
        COUNT(*) AS number_of_calls,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk
    FROM Calls
    GROUP BY city, HOUR(call_time)
)
SELECT 
    city, 
    peak_calling_hour, 
    number_of_calls
FROM CityHourCount
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY peak_calling_hour DESC, city DESC;
```

WITH CityHourCount AS (
    SELECT 
        city, 
        HOUR(call_time) AS peak_calling_hour, 
        COUNT(*) AS number_of_calls,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk
    FROM Calls
    GROUP BY city, HOUR(call_time)
)
SELECT 
    city, 
    peak_calling_hour, 
    number_of_calls
FROM CityHourCount
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY peak_calling_hour DESC, city DESC;

WITH CityHourCount AS (
    SELECT 
        city, 
        EXTRACT(HOUR FROM call_time)::INTEGER AS peak_calling_hour, 
        COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS number_of_calls,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk
    FROM Calls
    GROUP BY city, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM call_time)
)
SELECT 
    city, 
    peak_calling_hour, 
    number_of_calls
FROM CityHourCount
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY peak_calling_hour DESC, city DESC;
